registration_notes: pi-native-permissions module default is loaded by the actual native --extension argv. Its tool_call/session_start handlers register the native eight-tool definitions; permissionForTool and CONFIG_ENV are consumed internally.
host-profile renderClaudeNativePermissionSettings is consumed by the bounded Stage B qualification kit; it is not claimed as an automatic Claude configuration writer.
run/status/cancel/main and other existing CLI exports are consumed by native CLI entry and retained public dispatch; acp-conformance.runConformance is its require.main entry.
plugin-core exported installation methods remain adapter consumers; new Pi files are copied by the existing installDelegateAssets inventory and tested in isolated installations.

areas.anti_patterns: Inspected real worker spawn environment test and retained mutation RED/GREEN. Temporary child fixtures exercise actual launch and lifecycle boundaries.
areas.coverage_gaps: D1-AC01 through D1-AC05 map to task evidence, current 804 Node/104 Hook suite and native production observations. Windows execution and broader native versions are omitted explicitly.
areas.wiring: Collected changed module exports and inspected their native/shared consumers. No newly orphaned behavior found; internal helper exports are consumed within their module, not advertised as separate workflows.
areas.e2e: Retained native Pi production qualification NcFFGD and no-bootstrap public run 7XeasI prove legal write/read, typed final result, stopped boundary, plus denied actual effects in the qualification trial. No new provider trial needed for unchanged source.
areas.performance: Finite real provider runs and suite durations retained; no D1 throughput/latency threshold exists. Repeatable parallel-versus-solo performance belongs to C/D and remains unverified.
areas.security: Final release dependency audit0 plus exact runtime/config refusal, true worker env canaries, nested writer cancellation and native denied effects. Current cooperative file observations are not hostile OS containment.
